Class Dinosaur

java.lang.Object
gamemode.forest.entity.Dinosaur
Direct Known Subclasses:
CarnivoreDinosaur, HerbivoreDinosaur, MegaDinosaur
public abstract class Dinosaur extends Object
Abstract base class representing a dinosaur entity in the forest game mode.

Each dinosaur has combat stats, positional data, a rarity classification, and a limited lifetime after spawning. Subclasses must implement their own AI behavior via update(Player).

      public Dinosaur(String name, int hp, int strength, int expDrop, int requiredLevel, double x, double y, Dinosaur.Rarity rarity, String imagePath, double width, double height, double speed, int sellPrice)
      Constructs a new Dinosaur with the given attributes.
      Parameters:
      name - the display name of the dinosaur
      hp - the starting (and maximum) hit points
      strength - the attack strength; clamped to a minimum of 0
      expDrop - the experience rewarded on defeat; clamped to a minimum of 0
      requiredLevel - the minimum player level to encounter this dinosaur; clamped to a minimum of 1
      x - the initial X position in the game world
      y - the initial Y position in the game world

      imagePath - the resource path to the sprite image

      height - the height of the dinosaur's sprite
      speed - the movement speed in units per update tick
      sellPrice - the gold value when sold by the player

  • Method Details

    • update

      public abstract void update(Player player)
      Updates this dinosaur's behavior for the current game tick.

      Each subclass implements its own AI logic here, such as chasing, patrolling, or attacking the player.

      Parameters:
      player - the player entity to interact with

    • isExpired

      public boolean isExpired()
      Returns whether this dinosaur has exceeded its maximum lifetime.
      Returns:
      true if the dinosaur has been alive longer than LIFETIME

    • moveToward

      protected void moveToward(double targetX, double targetY)
      Moves this dinosaur one step toward the given target coordinates.

      Movement is normalized so the dinosaur always travels at exactly speed units per call, regardless of distance. Does nothing if the dinosaur is already at the target position.

      Parameters:
      targetX - the target X coordinate
      targetY - the target Y coordinate
